name: conduction_resistances_and_shapes
title: Conduction: thermal resistances, shape factors and R-value conversions (function library)
summary: Fourteen conduction relations as EES FUNCTIONs/PROCEDURE: plane-wall resistance <-> conductivity, thermal resistivity conversions, R-value <-> k in SI and imperial conventions, the cylindrical-wall resistance, the six isothermal conduction shape factors (sphere/pipe to plane, pipe normal to a plane, pipe to pipe, pipe between two planes, eccentric pipe in pipe) and the layered cylindrical-wall heat transfer with inner and outer convection coefficients (two layers, heat rate, overall coefficients and temperature profile).

authors: T. L. Bergman, A. S. Lavine, F. P. Incropera and D. P. DeWitt (Introduction to Heat Transfer, 6E)
F. Kreith, R. Manglik and M. Bohn (Principles of Heat Transfer)
J. E. Sunderland and K. R. Johnson (ASHRAE Transactions 70, 1964)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), file ht/conduction.py, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each relation is the book or paper cited in its function comment block (Bergman et al. 6E 2011, Kreith-Manglik-Bohn 2010, VDI Heat Atlas 2E 2010, Sunderland & Johnson 1964). Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: doctest values of ht 1.2.0 ht/conduction.py (case A) and additional values computed with the same ht functions in a throw-away virtualenv (case B); 50 output values in total

The 79 'only in CoolSolve' variables are the inputs of the demonstration program.
